title: I-VI. Immediate and mediate knowledge; vision; analogy; affirmation, negation, eminence
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): I. Now God by us either immediately or mediately is known. II. Immediately by clear vision of Him as He is, proper unto ye blessed in heaven. III. Mediately through analogical images plus signs — works plus word — through a mirror in an enigma, proper unto pilgrims. IV. Mediately from works or word in three modes: affirmation, negation plus eminence. V. Affirmation is ye first mode. VI. Negation removes imperfections; eminence raises perfections above creatures' manner.
pass_b_english: I. Now God is known by us either immediately or mediately.
II. Immediately, by clear vision of Him as He is (1 John 3:2; 1 Corinthians 13:12), proper to the blessed in heaven.
III. Mediately, through analogical images and signs — God's outward actions, works, and word (Psalm 19:1; Romans 1:20). This knowledge is called through a mirror in an enigma, proper to pilgrims.

IV. Mediately God is known from His works or word in three modes: affirmation, negation, and eminence. V. The first mode is affirmation. VI. Negation removes imperfections; eminence raises perfections above the manner of creatures.
source_text: I. Cognoscitur autem Deus a nobis immediate aut mediate. II. Immediate, per visionem claram ejus sicuti est, 1 Joh. 3.2; 1 Cor. 13.12, & beatorum propria est in caelis. III. Mediate, per imagines analogicas & signa, quae sunt actiones Dei externae & opera & verbum ipsius, Psal. 19.1; Rom. 1.20. Haec cognitio per speculum in aenigmate dicitur, & viatorum propria est. IV. Mediate cognoscitur Deus ex operibus aut verbo tribus modis: affirmationis, negationis & supereminentiae. V. Primus modus est affirmationis. VI. Negationis modus removet imperfectiones; supereminentiae elevat perfectiones supra creaturarum modum.
